tour.overview:
Rome has been lived in for almost 3,000 years, and nowhere shows it better than the valley between the Palatine and Capitoline hills. Here the Romans built the Forum, their market, law court and temple district, and the emperors raised palaces on the hill above and the Flavian Amphitheatre – the Colosseum – in the valley below. The historic centre of Rome has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1980.

This private day takes you through ancient Rome with a licensed guide and a car, so you never stand in a ticket line or wait for public transport in the heat. In the morning you visit the Colosseum, opened in the year 80 for up to 50,000 spectators, then the Arch of Constantine, the Roman Forum and the Palatine Hill. After a Roman lunch, the car takes you into the centre for the Pantheon, Piazza Navona and the Trevi Fountain, three places that show how the ancient city became the Rome of the popes and of Baroque artists.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 8 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Rome
• Type: private tour with licensed guide, car and driver
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy to moderate; about 6 km on uneven ancient paving and gravel, with some slopes

WHAT YOU SEE
• The Colosseum (first and second levels).
• The Arch of Constantine.
• The Roman Forum and the Via Sacra.
• The Palatine Hill and the view over the Circus Maximus.
• The Pantheon.
• Piazza Navona.
• The Trevi Fountain.

WHY THIS WORKS
We take the first Colosseum entry of the morning, before the heat and the big groups, and the car links the ancient sites with the centre so you save your legs for the places that matter.

WHO IT SUITS
First-time visitors to Rome, families with children who love gladiators, and anyone with only a few days in the city.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you are most interested in art and the popes, choose our Vatican Museums, Sistine Chapel and St Peter's tour.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
Colosseum tickets are personal: we need the full name of each traveller when you book, and you must carry an ID. Large bags and backpacks are not allowed in the Colosseum. There is little shade in the Forum and on the Palatine: bring a hat and water in summer.

days.name: Colosseum, Arch of Constantine, Roman Forum, Palatine Hill, Pantheon, Piazza Navona and Trevi Fountain
days.description:
What to expect: the great sights of ancient and Baroque Rome in one day, with a licensed guide, private car, timed tickets and lunch.

Your driver collects you at your hotel at about 8:30 and drops you at the Colosseum, where your guide is waiting with your timed tickets. The amphitheatre was begun by Emperor Vespasian around the year 70 on the site of Nero's private lake and opened by his son Titus in 80 with a hundred days of games. Inside, you stand on the first and second levels above the arena, look down into the underground passages where animals and gladiators waited for the lifts that raised them into the light, and learn how 50,000 Romans were seated by rank and let out in minutes through 80 numbered arches.

Outside, you pass the Arch of Constantine, raised in 315 to celebrate the emperor's victory at the Milvian Bridge, and enter the Roman Forum by the Via Sacra, the street of triumphal processions. You walk under the Arch of Titus, with its relief of the spoils of Jerusalem, past the Temple of Vesta, where the Vestal Virgins kept the sacred fire, the Senate House and the spot where Julius Caesar's body was burned in 44 BC. You then climb the Palatine Hill, where legend says Romulus founded the city and where the emperors built the palaces that gave us the word 'palace', and look down over the long oval of the Circus Maximus.

After lunch in a family-run trattoria – cacio e pepe, carbonara or saltimbocca – the car takes you to the centre. You step into the Pantheon, rebuilt by Hadrian around 125 and still covered by its original dome, 43 metres wide with an open eye at the top; Raphael is buried here. A short walk leads to Piazza Navona, built on the stadium of Domitian, with Bernini's Fountain of the Four Rivers, and you finish at the Trevi Fountain, completed in 1762, where tradition says a coin thrown over your shoulder brings you back to Rome. Your driver takes you back to your hotel at about 16:30.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
08:30 – Pick-up at your hotel.
09:00 – Colosseum (about 1 hour 15 minutes).
10:30 – Arch of Constantine and the Roman Forum.
11:30 – Palatine Hill and the view of the Circus Maximus.
12:45 – Lunch in a trattoria.
14:15 – Pantheon.
15:00 – Piazza Navona.
15:45 – Trevi Fountain.
16:30 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Access to the Colosseum arena floor and underground can be added on request, subject to availability.
• The Pantheon can close for religious services; we then visit at another time of the day.
• Pickpockets work the crowds at the Trevi Fountain: keep valuables in front of you.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, licensed guide, tickets to the Colosseum, Roman Forum, Palatine Hill and Pantheon, lunch, bottled water, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: Colosseum arena floor and underground, drinks with lunch, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Do we skip the lines at the Colosseum?
faq.answer: Yes. We book timed tickets in advance, so you skip the ticket line. Everyone still passes a short security check at the entrance.

faq.question: Are the entrance tickets included?
faq.answer: Yes: the Colosseum, Roman Forum and Palatine Hill, and the Pantheon. The arena floor and underground levels can be added on request.

faq.question: Why do you need our names?
faq.answer: Colosseum tickets are personal and are checked against ID at the entrance, so we need each traveller's full name when you book.

faq.question: Is there much walking?
faq.answer: About 6 km, mostly on ancient paving and gravel paths with some slopes on the Palatine. The car covers the distance between the ancient sites and the centre.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: Yes, a lunch of Roman classics in a trattoria. Vegetarian, gluten-free and other diets can be arranged.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Children love the gladiator stories and the coin at the Trevi Fountain. We adapt the pace and can shorten the Forum visit.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Partly. The Colosseum has a lift to the second level, but the Forum and the Palatine have uneven ground and slopes. Tell us your needs and we will adapt the route.

faq.question: Can we bring a backpack?
faq.answer: Small bags are fine. Large bags, backpacks and suitcases are not allowed in the Colosseum and there is no left-luggage there; you can leave them in the car.

faq.question: Can you pick us up at the cruise port?
faq.answer: Yes. From Civitavecchia the drive is about 1 hour 15 minutes each way, so the day is adapted to your ship's times and the price is confirmed with your request.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Comfortable shoes with good grip, a hat and sun protection in summer. For the Pantheon, which is a church, cover your shoulders.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: April to June and September to October. July and August are very hot, so we start early; winter is mild and much quieter.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
